newsitem.title: UK: Cardoso sees Brazil '97 inflation around 7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Cardoso sees Brazil '97 inflation around 7 pct.

text.p: Brazilian inflation is likely to continue to fall this year to around seven percent from an annual 10 percent in 1996, President Fernando Henrique Cardoso said on Monday.
"I hope in the current year...it will be no more than around seven percent," he told a conference.
He noted the country's Real plan had already slashed inflation of around 1,000 percent when it was introduced in 1994.
Cardoso said Brazil had carried out and consolidated profound changes, reforming the constitution and putting the economy increasingly in the hands of the private sector.
"Brazil faces the complex challenge of achieving fiscal equilibrium. I am certain that, with the support of Congress, we can make significant progress in the field, beginning this year," he said.
More work needed to be done to reduce inequality in the country, especially improving the performance of the public sector in areas such as education and health, he added.
